energy still at initial value just before collision at step 64
energy exceeds allowed 10%+5J tolerance at first violating step 65

counterfactual.change: Reduced dt from 0.02457 to 0.005 (only dt changed, same steps/bodies) to improve collision integration accuracy; energy stays conserved.

explanation: Elastic (e=1) circle-circle collision at large dt (0.0245) with high relative speed (~21 m/s) causes impulse integration error. Despite substepping (36 substeps), collision resolution adds spurious kinetic energy: energy jumps from 998J to 1131J after collision, exceeding 1103J limit. Smaller dt removes error, proving numerical cause.
vision_note: A small blue circle falls vertically toward a larger stationary blue circle. Around steps 64-65 they collide and the small circle rebounds, which in the strip appears as a sudden collision/bounce between the two free bodies with no wall present.
